title: Released CJP Leaders Vow Nationwide Protests, Escalating Standoff Over Voter Roll Revision
excerpt: Hours after a Delhi court released three CJP conveners from preventive custody, the group promised to take its demand for the Election Commission chief's resignation across the country — setting up a fresh confrontation with authorities.
body:
• CJP co-convener Ashutosh Ranka and leaders Saurav Das and Abhijeet Dipke were released on Sunday after being detained from inside a Delhi-bound aircraft on Saturday morning.
  • At a press conference hours after release, they vowed nationwide protests until Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resigns over the Special Intensive Revision of voter rolls.
  • At least 3,000 protesters were detained on Saturday — estimates ran as high as 7,000 — as police sealed 45 Delhi Metro stations and cancelled about 250 trains.
  • For travellers and families in Delhi: metro and rail services were reported normal again by Sunday; check DMRC and railway advisories before heading out on Monday, when the INDIA bloc plans its own march.

Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders vowed to widen their protest against alleged electoral fraud within hours of walking out of Delhi police custody on Sunday, a day after hundreds were detained trying to assemble near Jantar Mantar to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

"The fight has just begun," CJP co-convener Ashutosh Ranka said at a press conference. "This protest will not stop until Gyanesh resigns," he added, framing the campaign as the opening of a longer confrontation rather than a one-day show of force.

"The protests will happen not just in Delhi but the whole country," CJP leader Saurav Das said, directing his criticism at Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the BJP over what the party calls the misuse of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter rolls.

Detained from an aircraft, released by a magistrate

Ranka, Das and CJP chief Abhijeet Dipke were detained from inside an aircraft after their flight from Mumbai landed in Delhi on Saturday morning. Police placed them under preventive arrest and produced them before an executive magistrate in Delhi Cantonment on Sunday morning, who released them on the condition that they do not breach the peace for one year, according to police.

https://x.com/TheQuint/status/2109234821394297127

Ranka alleged the three had been "kidnapped" from the aircraft. He also accused the authorities of insensitivity in the way Dipke was informed of his grandmother's death while in detention; Dipke left for his hometown in Maharashtra immediately after release to attend her last rites.

The CJP maintains that no leader signed any bond promising to stop protesting. "Haven't signed any bond that says we won't protest. We will hit the streets again," Dipke posted on X, arguing that peaceful protest is a constitutional right and does not breach the peace.

"The protests will happen not just in Delhi but the whole country."

— Saurav Das, CJP leader

What the fight is actually about

At the centre of the dispute is the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls — a house-to-house verification exercise that deletes duplicates and dead or migrated voters. The Commission says it cleans the lists; the CJP and opposition parties allege it is being weaponised to disenfranchise voters and have demanded Gyanesh Kumar's resignation, a demand that drew thousands to Delhi on Saturday.

The scale of Saturday's crackdown was extraordinary even by the standards of the capital's protest politics. Police detained at least 3,000 people — some estimates went as high as 7,000 — threw a security ring around central Delhi, kept 45 metro stations closed and cancelled around 250 trains. (The Videshi's earlier reporting: Dhruv Rathee Detained, CJP Leaders Held as Delhi Blocks October 10 Jantar Mantar Protest.) Authorities told the Supreme Court on Sunday that metro and internet operations were back to normal, a point the court had pressed them on in a rare Sunday sitting over detentions and curbs (Supreme Court Bars Illegal Detentions, Orders Normal Metro and Internet in Delhi Protest Case).

YouTuber Dhruv Rathee was among those detained and released late on Saturday night. Student Federation of India leader Aishe Ghosh said, "Jantar Mantar 2.0 is on. We are on the streets; we will stay on the streets."

The other side responds

The BJP has dismissed the CJP as an arm of the opposition. BJP chief Nitin Nabin alleged the group was acting at the direction of "foreign forces" to hurt India. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta called the CJP the "B-team" of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal — Kejriwal was himself among four former chief ministers detained and released on Saturday.

Defence Minister Rajnath Singh struck a more measured note: "Every individual has the right to express dissent in a democracy," but people must not "forget that spreading anarchy is not anyone's right."

Diaspora angle

For the Indian diaspora watching from the US, UK, Canada and the Gulf, this is now the sharpest flashpoint yet in a months-long opposition campaign against the Election Commission's voter-roll exercise — one that has moved from parliament-adjacent rallies to mass detentions, court sittings and cancelled trains. The coming days will show whether the CJP's nationwide call finds feet beyond Delhi or burns out under the pressure of preventive arrests.

What's next

The CJP's leaders want Jantar Mantar opened as a protest venue and say protests will spread beyond Delhi this week. The INDIA bloc has separately announced a march in Delhi on Monday, October 12, to submit a memorandum to the Chief Justice. The immediate test is whether authorities permit Monday's assembly — or whether the capital sees a second straight week of metro closures and mass detentions.
